When Albert Einstein died in 1955, his brain went missing. For more than forty years.
Einstein wanted to be cremated, so that nobody would worship his remains.
But the doctor who did his autopsy, Thomas Harvey, quietly took the brain home.
He cut it into two hundred and forty pieces, and kept them in jars.
When people found out, he lost his job. But he kept the brain.
For decades, it moved house with him. At one point, it sat in a cider box, under a beer cooler.
Scientists who studied the pieces found some unusual features, but nothing that explained his genius.
In 1997, Harvey drove across America with the brain in the trunk, to meet Einstein's granddaughter.
A year later, he finally gave it back.
And Einstein's eyes? His eye doctor took those, and locked them in a bank vault in New York.
